# Worked example (test fixture, not a result)

The hand-computed case from [RFC-0004 §Worked example](../../../../../rfcs/0004-metrics-timing-grades.md#worked-example-test-fixture-not-a-result). The inputs are invented round numbers and describe no system. `inputs.json` holds the events, release times and recorded metrics; `expected.json` holds the values computed by hand in the RFC table. `run.json` is the same case as a run record whose derived values `iproofs derive --check` recomputes from their stored inputs, with `reference.yaml` (price 3.6 USD/gpu_hour, 1 GPU) and `workload.yaml` (8e9 active parameters, 8 weight bits) as fixture inputs. Tests compare with `math.isclose(rel_tol=1e-12)` because a decimal such as 0.01 has no exact binary64 form. The fixture holds `proofs_count` 5, so D-TPP (`tokens_covered_per_proof`) is 5,000 / 5 = 1,000 token (RFC-0004 worked example, D-TPP row). With 8e9 active parameters and 8 weight bits, D-SPAB-prove.steady (`seconds_per_active_weight_bit_token_prove.steady`) is 0.01 / (8.0e9 × 8) = 1.5625e-13 s/bit_token (RFC-0004 worked example, D-SPAB row).
